text:
maria.security: Heads up — security advisory for a credential-sync flaw we detected in a third-party task SaaS connector (TaskFlow). Short summary and immediate actions below.

jake.infra: what happened? impact?

maria.security: TaskFlow's latest webhook sync was writing job payloads that included temporary service tokens to an audit dump we ingest. We found a small sample (7 keys) in an internal archive. No public leak observed, but tokens may have propagated to TaskFlow accounts and their outbound integrations.

phil.security-engineering: can you confirm the tokens found are short-lived or long-lived?

maria.security: confirmed — 3 are long-lived service tokens (created pre-2025), 4 are ephemeral CI tokens. Long-lived ones are the priority.

ellen.platform: which teams own the affected tokens?

maria.security: affected tokens map: frontend-ci (2 ephemeral), data-pipeline-ingest (1 long-lived), model-batcher (2 long-lived), ops-alerts (1 ephemeral), analytics-exporter (1 ephemeral). I'll DM owners a list; please treat as org-wide.

maria.security: Immediate actions (TL;DR):
- Revoke the 3 long-lived tokens now.
- Rotate any service principal credentials that may include those tokens.
- Disable TaskFlow connector until TaskFlow confirms a fix OR we patch the connector to scrub at ingest.
- Search S3/archive for additional occurrences: key pattern "svc_" or regex "[A-Za-z0-9]{24}"
- Replace any CI usages and restart pipelines.

jake.infra: I'll run a search across our S3 prefixes and logs. Will also schedule rotation for model-batcher keys. ETA 90m.

maria.security: thanks. Priority order: model-batcher, data-pipeline-ingest, frontend-ci.

liam-sre: do we have an automated revocation playbook I can trigger?

ell en.platform: (typo) ellen.platform: we have the rotate-service-key tool, see gist: `curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/rotate -d \"service=model-batcher\"` — but do NOT run until infra confirms there are no active sessions that will cause outages.

phil.security-engineering: I'll open a formal incident ticket and flag for exec comms. Also asking legal to assess vendor contract obligations.

devops-bot: [alert] connector TaskFlow v2.3.1 flagged: PII/secret in webhook payloads — created ticket SEC-2026-081.

maria.security: Owner assignments:
- jake.infra -> run org-wide artifact search and post findings here (90m).
- ellen.platform -> schedule rotations and prepare minim downtime rotation plan (3h).
- liam-sre -> coordinate canary pipeline restarts and monitor errors (2h).
- phil.security-engineering -> incident ticket and vendor liaison.

jake.infra: search kickoff: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-archives --query 'Contents[?contains(Key, `taskflow`)]'` then `grep -E "svc_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"` — posting results in 45m.

ellen.platform: I'll prepare rotation runbook and update teams. Will use `rotate-service-key --force --no-restart` for non-prod first.

maria.security: Decision: temporarily disable TaskFlow connectors org-wide. Platform, please block connector via config flag.

ellen.platform: done — flag flipped in feature-config. TaskFlow connectors are disabled for prod and staging. Dev sandbox remains for debugging.

liam-sre: can we whitelist a debug window for infra to re-enable for 30m?

maria.security: yes — request in this thread with exact justification and time window. Approvals from phil and jake required.

phil.security-engineering: approved for a single 30m debug window, log all traffic and escalate on any unexpected outbound connections.

jake.infra: S3 scan partial results: found 9 matches total, 3 of which are the long-lived keys we flagged. I started rotation for model-batcher keys (in progress).

ellen.platform: rotations started for model-batcher and data-pipeline-ingest. Rolling restarts scheduled to avoid >5% capacity loss.

maria.security: ownership note: after rotation, owners must rotate any derived API integrations (TaskFlow, internal exporters). Patch request to TaskFlow submitted — they acknowledged and say a fix is scheduled for 48h.

phil.security-engineering: legal asked for vendor response SLA. I'm drafting a vendor incident timeline and sending to legal.

liam-sre: can we add an automated scrub in our ingestion pipeline ASAP? I can PR a middleware that redacts tokens matching `svc_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}`.

maria.security: please do. Prioritize non-breaking redaction and add metric for redaction hits.

ellen.platform: rotation complete for model-batcher and data-pipeline-ingest. Confirmed no downstream failures so far.

jake.infra: frontend-ci ephemerals rotated and pipelines restarted. No new matches in archive after 2nd pass.

maria.security: Excellent. Remaining actions:
- TaskFlow connector disabled until proof of fix (security).
- Add ingestion redaction middleware (liam).
- Run full archive scan nightly for 7 days (jake).
- Exec summary and postmortem (phil).

phil.security-engineering: I'll own the postmortem and exec communication. Draft will be ready EOD.

maria.security: Thanks everyone. If you touched keys, add a note to SEC-2026-081 with rotation commands used and CI tokens updated. Mark this advisory as "actioned" after all owners confirm in-thread.

ell en.platform: ellen.platform: marking model-batcher and data-pipeline-ingest as rotated in ticket.

liam-sre: PR for redact middleware opened: https://git.internal/redwood/platform/PR-432 — reviews welcome.

jake.infra: nightly scan job scheduled for next 7 days. Results will post to #sec-automations and this thread if any hits.

maria.security: Closure check in 24h. If no regressions or new findings, we'll move to post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
